chapter: Road life, arranging and racial dangers
title: Violence at White dances: Marlow and West Texas cowboys
summary: Booking agents sat at the door; a man attacked musicians in Marlow, cowboys demanded they keep playing, and Smith says they put it down to ignorance.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: ...sit right on the floor where the people were dancing. I remember, we was in Marlow, Oklahoma, a little town out there in the western part of Oklahoma, and we was playing a White dance. A little old fellow came by dancing with his girlfriend...with a lady; I guess it might have been his wife. But anyway, he come by there, haul off, and hit one of the boys in the (?) with his fists. He did that, and he tried to shove his trumpet down his throat. And the saxophone players, they'd be sitting there, and he went and kicked them on the leg. They'd be reading the music and playing, and he'd go on over and kick on the leg, trying to turn the stand over.
Would this be a young guy or an older guy?

Well, he looked to be about 30-35 years old. And our booking agent, he was on the door -- he was a White man. So we told him about it, and he had to get off the door and put somebody else on the door, and come back there and take care of the band.
Buster Smith - 55
So your booking agent would travel with you.
Yeah.
I see. Always.

Uh-huh. Sometimes we'd play out in the West...in some of the Western towns, way out in West Texas out there, some cowboys would come in there and they didn't want to let us quit playing. You got to play til they say "Stop."
They came in with their guns out...
Yeah. And the only way the band could get away a lot of times, we had to go out the back door. Step out one at a time. All that kind of stuff.
Oh, wow!
Yeah.
Did it ever happen to you as a band or bands you knew that actually the band would get beaten up or get (?) out of town?

No. Wouldn't hardly none of 'em get beat in (?) because they'd go along with them until they'd get out of town, if you had to hurry and get out of town and all that kind of stuff. You wouldn't get beat up. You had to go along with 'em until you could get away from there.
God, it must have really made you hate them.
No. We just figured that people were just ignorant, just didn't know any better.
Well, that, of course, is a very mature way of looking at
Buster Smith - 56
it.
Yes. Uh-huh.
I'm amazed you were that philosophical, frankly.
Yeah. See, news like that travels fast, you know.
Stay out of that town.
Yeah. Uh-huh.
